interpolation.comment: ${ ... } -- the only interpolation syntax there is, in text, in CSS and in attribute values alike
interpolation.name: meta.embedded.expression.markout

directive-close-tag.comment: </:define>, </:group>, ... -- matched before the open tag, so that the `<` of a `</` never starts one

directive-tag.comment: <:import>, <:include>, <:define>, <:slot>, <:group>, <:logic> -- tags HTML doesn't know, so it leaves their attributes unpainted and we do them ourselves. It runs to the closing `>` as a block, both to reach those attributes and to give the tag a meta.tag scope: that's what the inter-attribute comments inject into.
directive-tag.name: meta.tag.directive.markout

colon-attribute.comment: the attributes HTML has no name for: values, class and style toggles, events, lifecycle, replication. A block rather than a bare name, so the `=` and the value that follows are ours too -- left to HTML they are characters it thinks are illegal there
colon-attribute.name: meta.attribute.markout
